To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
frzb2 is involved in the regulation of anterior development and sizzled is involved in the modulation of ventral development in Xenopus.
frzb2 and Sizzled2 have different roles during Xenopus development.

two members of the frizzeld-related proteins (frps) frzb2 and Sizzled2 have distinct activities on anterior patterning. frzb2 acts as an inhibitor of XWnt8 activity and thus inhibits head formation, while Sizzled2 does not inhibit Wnt activity, but instead dorsalizes embryos, leading to an expansion of the anterior head.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Frzb2 and Sizzled2 are antagonistic factors that modulate the activity of Wnts in the anterior region of the embryo.
the FRPs, in particular frzb2 and Sizzled2, are important modulators of Wnt signaling and that they may be used to manipulate Wnt activity in vivo.
Frzb2 inhibits Wnt8 and Wnt8 is required for anterior ectoderm development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Wnt signaling pathways are not as simple as they are often described.
the two Frizzled-related genes we have studied, frzb2 and Sizzled2, have antagonistic roles in A/P patterming, but they do so by different mechanisms.
frzb2 and Xwnt8 act together in head mesodermal cells, whereas sizzled2 and Xwnts act together in the ectoderm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the different activities of frz2 and sizz2 are not simply a result of differential binding of the proteins to Xwnt8.
there are different types of Wnt antagonists that can have different activities during development.
there is more to Wnt signaling than just the Wnt ligands.
